text:
maya: heads-up — we've got p99 latency spikes (~180ms extra) on g5x since driver 535.12 rolled out. noticed this on canary and Prod: short-seq traffic (seq_len <= 32) seems hit hardest. profiler shows kernel selector choosing a naive GEMM path instead of flash-attn in a bunch of requests. attaching quick profiler paste.

maya: ```
shape: B=8, S=16, H=4096, head=64
kernel choice: matmul_gemm_nv + kv_merge (fallback)
flash_attn expected latency: 6.2ms
actual chosen path latency: 18.7ms
callstack: kernel_select -> triton_autoselect -> matmul_dispatcher
notes: memcopy stalls ~12%
```

kevin: do we have driver + cudnn versions for the affected hosts?

maya: all g5x nodes are on driver 535.12 + cuda 12.3 image (same as rollout). non-g5x nodes (a100) are fine.

perf-bot: alert: latency_regression detected on route /v1/stream (p99 +27% over baseline). top contributing hosts: g5x-03,g5x-07,g5x-12.

sanjay: hmm, driver bump might change kernel occupancy heuristics used by Triton/our autoselector. Did the selector detect different SM availability or shared mem size?

rachel: I replayed a short-seq workload on a repro host and ran nsight: SM util lower and we see frequent fallback to `matmul_gemm_nv` for tiny S. nvprof shows higher L2 miss rate too. looks like the kernel benchmark numbers triton uses got skewed by the driver perf counters.

anton: can we force flash-attn path for a small percentage of traffic to confirm perf delta? we should also check KV cache alignment — small sequences + KV sharding might cause odd memory shapes that hit a different code path.

kevin: +1 for canary. rachel — can you add a route override or set KERNEL_SELECTOR=force_flashattn on one canary host?

rachel: doing that now on g5x-03, routing 5% traffic. will post numbers in 10m.

maya: quick sanity checks: 1) kernel selector thresholds in triton-config changed? 2) flash-attn kernel now compiled with different sm/flags? 3) driver perf counters remap -> affects autotuner.

rachel: found a clue — the autotuner uses a microbenchmark that measures throughput for S=16 but it times out early if memcpy latency spikes are >10ms; driver 535 seems to report memcpy slightly slower for pinned pages on g5x, causing autotuner to prefer the GEMM path for those shapes.

sanjay: so it's not flash-attn failing at runtime, it's the selector's benchmarking being biased by driver-level memcpy numbers. that would flip preferred kernel even though flash-attn still beats in real load.

perf-bot: test results available: canary g5x-03 (force_flashattn) p99 dropped back to baseline within 5m. throughput stable.

rachel: canary numbers: baseline p99 ~320ms, regress p99 ~500ms, force_flashattn p99 ~335ms. detailed trace shows 12ms -> 5ms on kernel hotpath.

kevin: great repro. next steps? patch selector to discount memcpy from microbench for small seqs, and add secondary check that compares real-request latency before committing new kernel choice.

anton: also add a quick guard: if flash-attn was chosen in production previously for shape X, and new autotune flips, sanity-check against historical perf window before rollout.

maya: agree. we should also add a CI microbenchmark that runs under driver 535 image to catch autotuner sensitivity.

rachel: I'll open two PRs: 1) tweak autotuner to ignore memcpy spikes for S <= 32, 2) add historical-backstop check + unit test. linking in thread when open.

sanjay: filing incident ticket to rollback selector rollout on g5x fleet until fix lands? or we can patch selector server-side without rollback.

kevin: prefer quick server-side guard rollout (hotfix) to avoid infra churn. if that looks hairy, rollback.

maya: ok plan: rachel opens PRs, we deploy server-side guard (set min_score_delta threshold and historical check) to prod canary 10% then expand. if expansion mirrors earlier regression, rollback. assign owners: rachel -> PRs, sanjay -> rollout guard, kevin -> monitor and rollback plan, anton -> perf CI.

rachel: PRs opened: #4123 (autotune tweak), #4124 (historical guard). debug notes and benchmark attached in PRs.

perf-bot: incident created: INC-2026-1193, priority P2.

kevin: thanks everyone. big win that force_flashattn brought latency down — seems confirmed selector heuristics were tripped by driver-level memcpy measurements.

maya: leaving this thread open until guards are in prod and canary looks good. please post rollouts and any surprising diffs. :thumbsup:
